From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: QBR cover story + risk appendix — draft + pulls for OKR check-ins

Team — kicking off a short sprint to finalize the investor-facing QBR cover and a concise risk appendix. Goal: have a board-ready draft to share with ScaleBridge by EOD Friday so they can preview before the July 8 meeting.

What I attached: 20260630_QBR_cover_and_risks_v0.3.pptx (high-level cover + one-slide risk appendix) and a raw OKR pull (Q2_OKR_progress_summary.xlsx).

Asks:
- Laura: can you lead narrative voice on the cover (3 bullets + topline metric callouts)? Prefer a one-paragraph cover story + two visual metrics.
- Marcus: supply final revenue ARR and usage delta cells from June month-end by Thursday 12pm PT so I can call out growth vs plan.
- Neha: reconcile the OKR status semantics — we need consistent "On Track / At Risk / Missed" mapping and a single line for each cross-functional risk we plan to include in the risk appendix.
- Stephanie: coordinate a single source of truth for attachments + run a short editorial pass (tone + slide sizing).

Quick constraints: keep the risk appendix to 4 bullets max; each risk bullet should have an owner and a mitigation line (12 words max). We will iterate quickly in thread — please reply inline.

Timeline:
- Thu 12:00 PT: Marcus numbers in
- Thu 5:00 PT: internal review freeze (Irene)
- Fri EOD: preview to ScaleBridge (Anna)

Thanks,
Irene

Looks good. Slide 2 (cover hero) needs a tighter headline — propose: "Predictable Inference: Lower Cost, Higher Availability" (we can iterate).

> Laura: can you lead narrative voice on the cover (3 bullets + topline metric callouts)?
Yes. I'll draft three crisp bullets and call out: ARR growth (YoY%), GPU utilization change, and latency SLO attainment.

Draft asks for Marcus: please confirm ARR and active seat metrics; if we have a 90-day rolling MAU/Requests number, include that too so the cover can show both revenue and usage momentum.

Risk appendix (initial language suggestions):
- Supply: GPU capacity pressure during peak enterprise onboarding — Owner: Infra Ops (Mitigation: Dedicated pools + prioritized routing)
- Quality drift: Regression from new model variants — Owner: Applied ML (Mitigation: Eval guardrails + canary rollouts)
- Procurement/contract: Extended legal timelines for enterprise customers — Owner: Sales Ops (Mitigation: Standardized SLA playbook)
- Data residency: Region-specific metadata retention requirements — Owner: Security (Mitigation: VPC private control plane)

I'll take the first pass on cover copy and attach v0.4 by Thu 3pm PT for editorial.

Laura

Thanks — I reconciled the OKR semantics and updated the spreadsheet: mapping used is "On Track / At Risk / Missed / Achieved". I added the single-line owner+mitigation for cross-functional risks in the "Risks_for_deck" tab. Copy below that I recommend for the risk appendix (short, board-friendly):

1) GPU availability: Infra Ops — provisioning cadence and dedicated pools to prioritize enterprise bursts.
2) Model regressions: Applied ML — automatic evals + staged rollouts to catch quality drift.
3) Contracting cadence: Sales Ops — playbook + procurement checklist to reduce legal lead time.
4) Data sovereignty: Security — region-specific retention & private control plane options.

I also flagged two OKRs as "At Risk" where we may need a short mitigation note in the narrative:
- OKR: Reduce per-token cost by 12% — status: At Risk (billing alignment & model config changes behind schedule)
- OKR: Launch EU private tenancy pilot — status: At Risk (networking certs delayed)

I'll be available for a 30-min walk-through Thu 4:00 PT if you want to go slide-by-slide.

Neha Kapoor
Dir, Governance & Risk, Redwood Inference
